From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Hi all — agile technical reply with the test plan we used for similar customers. High level first, then concrete artifacts.

Executive summary (topline):
- Synthetic traffic shapes: Poisson baseline, scheduled diurnal (3x peak/valley), and head-filling bursts (sawtooth with 30s super-peak every 5m).
- Typical results (single quantized 13B model on 80GB A100 equivalent): sustained tokens/sec per GPU = ~1100–1300 (depends on decode settings). p95 generation latency at 256-token seq ≈ 120–180ms; p99 ≈ 240–420ms; 99.9 ≈ 520–900ms under sustained 8k RPS burst mix.
- Cold vs warm: cold container start (fresh model load) adds ~8–12s once-per-container; KV/prefix cache warming requires ~5000 short prefix requests to stabilize p99 by ~30–40%. We use a proactive prefix-warm policy in production.
- Autoscale behavior: our default policy is target-p95 < 250ms with hysteresis. Scale-up trigger: sustained p95 > 250ms for 60s OR GPU util > 85% for 90s. Scale-down: p95 < 180ms for 5m and util < 60%. Typical time-to-provision (add GPU) in Dedicated is ~90–140s; for Hosted with burst-pools we can have cold capacity within ~60s via warm standby. Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to a smaller variant (quantized 6B) with preserved response format when primary cannot meet latency SLOs.

Test harness and methodology (artifacts attached):
- Harness: Locust driver + custom tokenizer-aware client to model think-time and streaming. We include a JMeter profile for deterministic runs.
- Traffic shapes: Poisson lambda sweep (10–10k RPS), step increases (30s, 2x, 5x), and long soak (6h at target RPS).
- Observability: per-request tracing ID, GPU utilization sampling (nvidia-smi intervals), token throughput counters, per-batch latency breakdown (model_compute, kernel_copy, queuing, network).
- Priming: We seed KV/prefix cache by replaying 10k representative short queries; we also run a 10-minute warm soak at 20% target RPS prior to measurement windows.
- Determinism: runs are repeated 3x; we report median and the envelope (min/max) and variance.

Attachments included: stress-matrix.xlsx (run matrix), run-harness.tar.gz (locust + scripts), topline-results-95-99.csv (sample outputs). Also linking a condensed runbook PDF for procurement.

Notes / recommendations for Zephyr:
- If you expect very spiky enterprise bursts (sub-1min spikes), request provisioned burst capacity (warm standby) to avoid cold-start penalties.
- Use prefix-caching for commonly used prompts (we can provide profiling to identify top-k prefixes).
- Consider quantization to int8 for cost-sensitive workloads; benchmark shows ~1.6x throughput improvement with 5–10% p99 latency increase for aggressive quantization on some models.

I’ll attach the artifacts shortly. Happy to hop on the technical call to walk through results and tune the matrix to your production mix.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: stress-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet); run-harness.tar.gz (tarball); topline-results-95-99.csv (CSV)
